outcome.description: You close the gap. The transport's beacon flickers off. Two armed ships you didn't see drop out of stealth.
The drive readouts are wrong for a civilian. Heat blooms behind the transport tell you there are escorts holding station. You veer off, mark the coordinates for patrol, and burn clean.
The scans look fine. You commit. The trap closes.
You log the coordinates and keep your heading. If she was real, she'll wait. If she wasn't, the next ship that passes will learn.
You dock. The pilot wasn't a pilot. The rig was a shell. Two skiffs unhide from behind it.
The diagnostic comes back clean. His drive is fine. You acknowledge the call, say you're sending coordinates to a tow, and burn out before he can answer.
The remote diagnostic times out. You can't tell from here. You commit and dock.
You hold your line. The rig fades behind you.
You move into formation. He flies clean for thirty seconds. Then his weapons rotate to your side and three other ships uncloak.
His ID returns no record. You decline the escort, mark the cutter for patrol, and put distance between you.
The check times out. You decide to trust the badge.
He thanks you, professional and clipped. The cutter falls behind. You don't look back.
You close range. The relay's broadcast cuts. A masked transponder lights up behind it and a second one pings off your starboard. Ambush.
The carrier resolves into a forged signature. You tag the relay coordinates for patrol, and steer wide. Patrol confirms the find a day later. They cut you in for the bounty.
The decode runs slow. By the time you have the answer, you're already inside the kill zone.
You log the relay's coordinates and burn past. Whatever it was, it isn't your problem this hour.
